observations: A large skull-like form fills the center, drawn in heavy black outlines with a mouth showing irregular white teeth along the upper row and pink-purple marks along the lower gums, framed by dark interior space between the rows.
Bright cerulean blue dominates the background, crossed by a dark grid of thin lines at upper right, with yellow cloud-like patches and small white diamond shapes scattered at left.

The eye areas contain layered circles—yellow spirals, red slashes, white crosshatching on the left; yellow ring and purple grid on the right—topped by a jagged row of yellow triangles across the brow.
reading: The skull sits frontal, its uneven white teeth and dark jaw gap reading as a grin or a howl. Yellow spikes along the forehead and red marks inside the eye circles lend a feeling of alarm. The saturated blue field pushes tangled black outlines forward, making every scrawled layer compete for attention. Small diamond shapes at left feel like stray signals, quiet against the roar of the central form.
contextAngle: Within the owned rawblocks subset, this work sits between #58 and #60. All three neighbors feature skull-like heads, but #59 stands apart with its flat cerulean ground and single dominant figure, while #58 uses a brown field and #60 crowds multiple figures together.

connections.reason: Both share a bright blue background and a single round skull form, but nnotb #173 fills its eye areas with a heart and a flower, softening the face compared to #59's red slashes.
Rawblocks #58 repeats the heavy black skull outline and exposed teeth but swaps the blue field for olive-brown and adds green heart shapes absent from #59.

lookingQuestion: How do the small white diamond shapes at the left edge relate to the dense, tangled marks inside the skull—do they feel like fragments escaping the head, or something arriving from outside it?
ambiguities: Characters or numbers appear inside the mouth area but are partially obscured by overlapping strokes, making them difficult to read with certainty.
A pink vertical stripe along the left jaw could be a separate element or part of the skull's outline; layering makes the boundary unclear.
